chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Amr ibn Uthman, from one of his companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I heard him saying: 'A man commits a sin, and Allah enters him into Paradise because of it.' I said: 'Does Allah enter him into Paradise because of the sin?' He said: 'Yes. He commits a sin, so he does not cease to be fearful of it, hating his own self, so Allah shows mercy on him and enters him into Paradise.'
ai.seo_question: How can a sin lead to Paradise in Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi illustrates the Shia concept of 'good consequences of bad deeds' (hasanāt al-dhunūb), where the spiritual benefit arises not from the sin itself, but from the resulting humility and fear of God (khawf) that prevents arrogance. The Imam clarifies that the sin acts as a catalyst for self-reproach (muqātāt al-nafs), which purifies the believer and earns divine mercy, ultimately leading to Paradise.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Amro Bin Usman, from one of his companions, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>, said, ‘I heard him<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The man commits the sin so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Enters him into the Paradise due to it’. I said, ‘Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Enters him into the Paradise due to the sin?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Yes. He commits a sin, so he does not cease to be fearful from it, disliking his self, so Allah<sup>azwj</sup> shows Mercy on him and Enters him into the Paradise’.
en.sarwar: 3. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ‘Umar (‘Amr) ibn ‘Uthman from certain individuals of his people who has said the following:

“I heard abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) saying, ‘A man commits a sin and because of it Allah will admit him in paradise.’ I asked, ‘Will Allah admit him in paradise because of his sin?’ The Imam said, ‘Yes, he commits a sin and continues living in fear, and angry on his own self. Allah then grants him mercy and admits him in paradise.’”
